items.title: Jake Hanna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997
items.q: When Kenny Davern starts playing, now the time starts swinging.

ctx.x: Well you said, “To me freedom is gained through limiting your playing, disciplining yourself. Some modern drummers don’t play with license.”

They play with reckless abandon I guess they call it. Arthritic abandon, that’s what they call it. Arthritic abandon. Oh they were too busy. Too much noise going on you know. You eliminate all that and you get the good feeling, right with the bass, get the piano player to stay out of the way, and the horn player’s got a chance. Now if he starts playing too busy, get another horn player, you know. You can hear the difference. When Kenny Davern starts playing, now the time starts swinging. It starts swinging man,…
don’t fluff it off by saying oh you either swing or you don’t. It isn’t that easy. You have to think about the thing. Concentrate. A lot of concentration.
